ai.description: This stout snake grows to 60–100 cm. It is uniform grass-green to olive with a yellow-white belly and a distinctive black-bordered yellow collar behind the head. It lacks venom fangs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Green Keelback is best identified by its uniform, unpatterned leaf-green body and a distinct, dark "V" or "Y" shaped mark on the nape of its neck.
ai.habitat: The Green Keelback inhabits moist deciduous forests, scrublands, and grasslands across the Indian subcontinent, typically ranging from sea level to 2,000 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Green Keelback flattens its neck and raises its forebody in a cobra-like hood display to appear larger to potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhabdophis plumbicolor* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–15 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatching following in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Green Keelback is found across the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the Western Ghats, the Deccan Plateau, and parts of the Himalayas, ranging from sea level to 2,000m.
